references.text: Moses asks God not to destroy the people after the golden calf incident at Horeb, parallel to the anger of God mentioned in Deuteronomy 9:8
Israel's rebellion at Horeb (Massah and Meribah) where the people tested the Lord and provoked his anger
The Lord's anger burned against the people because of their complaints, and fire consumed them—an example of God's wrath toward Israel
Moses describes how he feared the Lord's burning anger, with which He intended to destroy the people
The psalm recounts the event at Horeb where Israel made a calf and aroused God's anger so that He wanted to destroy them
Ezekiel refers to laws that were not good, given because of Israel's rebellion—linked to God's judgment on the people
Hebrews warns against hardening the heart as at Meribah, and refers to God's anger toward that generation in the wilderness
